blocks.en: Introduction: The Apostle to the Nations
blocks.es_reference: Introducción: El Apóstol a las Naciones

blocks.en: After the Lord Jesus Himself, no one in history has shaped the work of world missions like the apostle Paul. He was the first great cross-cultural missionary, the model church-planter, and the theologian who explained to the church why the gospel must go to all nations. In roughly fifteen years of labor he carried the gospel across Asia Minor and into Europe, planted churches in city after city, and wrote letters that still instruct and convict the people of God today. To study missions is, in large part, to study Paul. In this unit we trace his call, his sending, his journeys, his strategy, his suffering, and his message.
blocks.es_reference: Después del Señor Jesús mismo, nadie en la historia ha dado forma a la obra de las misiones mundiales como el apóstol Pablo. Fue el primer gran misionero transcultural, el modelo del plantador de iglesias, y el teólogo que explicó a la iglesia por qué el evangelio debe ir a todas las naciones. En unos quince años de labor llevó el evangelio por Asia Menor y hasta Europa, plantó iglesias en ciudad tras ciudad, y escribió cartas que todavía instruyen y convencen al pueblo de Dios hoy. Estudiar las misiones es, en gran parte, estudiar a Pablo. En esta unidad trazamos su llamado, su envío, sus viajes, su estrategia, su sufrimiento y su mensaje.

blocks.en: I. The Persecutor Turned Missionary
blocks.es_reference: I. El Perseguidor Convertido en Misionero

blocks.en: Paul did not begin as a friend of the gospel. He began as its fiercest enemy, a one-man inquisition breathing threats and murder against the disciples. But on the road to Damascus the risen Christ stopped him with a flash of noonday light, and the persecutor became the preacher. From the very first moment, his commission was a missionary commission. The Lord said of him, "He is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My name before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel" (Acts 9:15, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: Pablo no comenzó como amigo del evangelio. Comenzó como su más feroz enemigo, una inquisición de un solo hombre que respiraba amenazas y muerte contra los discípulos. Pero en el camino a Damasco el Cristo resucitado lo detuvo con un destello de luz de mediodía, y el perseguidor se volvió predicador. Desde el primer momento, su comisión fue una comisión misionera. El Señor dijo de él: "Instrumento escogido me es éste, para llevar mi nombre en presencia de los gentiles, y de reyes, y de los hijos de Israel" (Hechos 9:15, RVG).

blocks.en: Two lessons stand out from that conversion. First, nobody is too far gone. The same Christ who made a Paul out of a Saul still walks the roads of this world looking for hardened sinners; no one is beyond His reach. Second, conversion costs the convert. The Lord did not promise Saul comfort; He promised him suffering: "For I will show him how many things he must suffer for My name's sake" (Acts 9:16, NKJV). The gospel is the costliest free gift in the universe, and a faithful missionary tells men the price on the front end.
blocks.es_reference: Dos lecciones se destacan de aquella conversión. Primero, nadie está demasiado perdido. El mismo Cristo que hizo un Pablo de un Saulo todavía recorre los caminos de este mundo buscando a los pecadores endurecidos; nadie está fuera de su alcance. Segundo, la conversión le cuesta al convertido. El Señor no le prometió a Saulo comodidad; le prometió sufrimiento: "Porque yo le mostraré cuán grandes cosas le es necesario que padezca por mi nombre" (Hechos 9:16, RVG). El evangelio es el regalo gratuito más costoso del universo, y un misionero fiel le dice al hombre el precio desde el principio.

blocks.en: II. Sent by the Church
blocks.es_reference: II. Enviado por la Iglesia

blocks.en: Paul did not send himself. As we saw in the last unit, it was the church at Antioch that laid hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them out under the leading of the Holy Spirit. And here a third lesson from his early days deserves our attention: the church needs its Barnabases. When the disciples in Jerusalem were still afraid of the former persecutor, it was Barnabas who took him in and vouched for him. There are more Barnabas-shaped roles in any congregation than there will ever be Paul-shaped pulpits, and the future of the gospel often runs through the people willing to stand behind a new believer who has no reputation yet.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo no se envió a sí mismo. Como vimos en la unidad anterior, fue la iglesia de Antioquía la que impuso las manos sobre Bernabé y Saulo y los envió bajo la dirección del Espíritu Santo. Y aquí una tercera lección de sus primeros días merece nuestra atención: la iglesia necesita a sus Bernabés. Cuando los discípulos en Jerusalén todavía temían al ex perseguidor, fue Bernabé quien lo acogió y respondió por él. Hay más papeles con forma de Bernabé en cualquier congregación de los que jamás habrá púlpitos con forma de Pablo, y el futuro del evangelio muchas veces corre por medio de los que están dispuestos a respaldar a un nuevo creyente que aún no tiene reputación.

blocks.en: Paul never worked alone. He labored with Barnabas, then with Silas, with young Timothy, with Luke the physician, and with Priscilla and Aquila. Missions, in Paul's hands, was always the work of a team sent by a church.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo nunca trabajó solo. Trabajó con Bernabé, luego con Silas, con el joven Timoteo, con Lucas el médico, y con Priscila y Aquila. Las misiones, en manos de Pablo, fueron siempre la obra de un equipo enviado por una iglesia.

blocks.en: III. The Three Journeys
blocks.es_reference: III. Los Tres Viajes

blocks.en: Paul's life as a missionary is usually traced through three great journeys. On the first, he and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus and then crossed into the highlands of Galatia, preaching in Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe, and planting churches in the face of fierce opposition. On the second journey, God closed the door into Asia and gave Paul a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading, "Come over and help us." With that vision the gospel crossed into Europe — to Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea, Athens, and eighteen fruitful months in Corinth. On the third journey Paul settled for nearly three years in Ephesus, until the word of the Lord had sounded throughout the whole province of Asia. The arc of his life ran ever westward, ever toward new ground.
blocks.es_reference: La vida de Pablo como misionero suele trazarse a través de tres grandes viajes. En el primero, él y Bernabé navegaron a Chipre y luego cruzaron a las tierras altas de Galacia, predicando en Antioquía de Pisidia, Iconio, Listra y Derbe, y plantando iglesias frente a una feroz oposición. En el segundo viaje, Dios cerró la puerta a Asia y dio a Pablo una visión de un varón macedonio que rogaba: "Pasa a Macedonia y ayúdanos." Con aquella visión el evangelio cruzó a Europa — a Filipos, Tesalónica, Berea, Atenas, y dieciocho fructíferos meses en Corinto. En el tercer viaje Pablo se estableció por casi tres años en Éfeso, hasta que la palabra del Señor hubo resonado por toda la provincia de Asia. El arco de su vida corrió siempre hacia el occidente, siempre hacia terreno nuevo.

blocks.en: IV. Paul's Missionary Strategy
blocks.es_reference: IV. La Estrategia Misionera de Pablo

blocks.en: Paul's labors were not random; he worked by a clear strategy that missionaries still learn from. He went to the great cities — Antioch, Ephesus, Corinth, Philippi — strategic centers from which the gospel could radiate into the surrounding region. He began in the synagogue, taking the gospel to the Jew first, and when he was rejected he turned to the Gentiles. He planted churches, appointed elders to lead them, and moved on, returning later or writing letters to strengthen them. Above all, he aimed at unreached ground: "And so I have made it my aim to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build on another man's foundation" (Romans 15:20, NKJV). The regions beyond were always before him.
blocks.es_reference: Las labores de Pablo no fueron al azar; trabajó con una estrategia clara de la cual los misioneros todavía aprenden. Iba a las grandes ciudades — Antioquía, Éfeso, Corinto, Filipos — centros estratégicos desde los cuales el evangelio podía irradiar a la región circundante. Comenzaba en la sinagoga, llevando el evangelio al judío primero, y cuando era rechazado se volvía a los gentiles. Plantaba iglesias, nombraba ancianos para dirigirlas, y seguía adelante, regresando más tarde o escribiendo cartas para fortalecerlas. Sobre todo, apuntaba a terreno no alcanzado: "Y de esta manera me esforcé a predicar el evangelio, no donde Cristo ya hubiese sido nombrado, por no edificar sobre fundamento ajeno" (Romanos 15:20, RVG). Las regiones más allá siempre estaban delante de él.

blocks.en: V. The Cost of the Mission
blocks.es_reference: V. El Costo de la Misión

blocks.en: The missionary life of Paul was watered with tears. He could remind the Ephesian elders that for three years he did not cease to warn everyone night and day with tears (Acts 20:31). And it was a life marked by suffering. He was imprisoned often, beaten beyond measure, given the thirty-nine lashes five times, shipwrecked, and exposed to danger on every side, carrying daily the weight of his care for all the churches (2 Corinthians 11:23–28). Yet he never counted the cost too high. "I have become all things to all men, that I might by all means save some" (1 Corinthians 9:22, NKJV). The true missionary spends himself for the souls of others.
blocks.es_reference: La vida misionera de Pablo fue regada con lágrimas. Pudo recordar a los ancianos de Éfeso que por tres años no había cesado de amonestar con lágrimas a cada uno, de noche y de día (Hechos 20:31). Y fue una vida marcada por el sufrimiento. Fue encarcelado muchas veces, azotado sin medida, recibió los treinta y nueve azotes cinco veces, naufragó, y estuvo expuesto al peligro por todos lados, llevando cada día el peso de su preocupación por todas las iglesias (2 Corintios 11:23–28). Sin embargo, nunca tuvo el costo por demasiado alto. "A todos me he hecho todo, para que de todos modos salve a algunos" (1 Corintios 9:22, RVG). El verdadero misionero se gasta a sí mismo por las almas de los demás.

blocks.en: VI. The Theologian of the Mission
blocks.es_reference: VI. El Teólogo de la Misión

blocks.en: Paul did not only labor in the mission; he explained it. In his letter to the Romans he laid bare the lostness of every man and the gospel that is for every nation, and he pressed the church with the unanswerable logic of sending: "How shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach unless they are sent?" (Romans 10:14–15, NKJV). In his letter to the Galatians he defended the gospel of grace for the Gentiles against all who would burden them with the law, insisting that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek. His letters are the missionary's deepest schooling, and the church has never outgrown them.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo no solo trabajó en la misión; la explicó. En su carta a los Romanos puso al descubierto la perdición de todo hombre y el evangelio que es para toda nación, y apremió a la iglesia con la lógica incontestable del envío: "¿Cómo oirán sin haber quien les predique? ¿Y cómo predicarán si no fueren enviados?" (Romanos 10:14–15, RVG). En su carta a los Gálatas defendió el evangelio de la gracia para los gentiles contra todos los que querían cargarlos con la ley, insistiendo en que en Cristo no hay judío ni griego. Sus cartas son la escuela más profunda del misionero, y la iglesia nunca las ha superado.

blocks.en: Conclusion: A Life Poured Out
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión: Una Vida Derramada

blocks.en: Paul shows us what a life poured out for the nations looks like: called by grace, sent by a praying church, strategic in his labor, joyful in his suffering, and clear in his gospel. At the end he could write, "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7, NKJV). The same Lord who made a missionary out of the persecutor of Tarsus is still calling and still sending. The only question is whether He will find in us the willing heart He found in Paul.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo nos muestra cómo es una vida derramada por las naciones: llamada por la gracia, enviada por una iglesia que ora, estratégica en su labor, gozosa en su sufrimiento, y clara en su evangelio. Al final pudo escribir: "He peleado la buena batalla, he acabado la carrera, he guardado la fe" (2 Timoteo 4:7, RVG). El mismo Señor que hizo un misionero del perseguidor de Tarso todavía está llamando y todavía está enviando. La única pregunta es si hallará en nosotros el corazón dispuesto que halló en Pablo.

sa.prompt: Describe Paul's conversion on the Damascus road and explain how his commission was missionary from the start.
sa.model: On the road to Damascus, the risen Christ stopped Paul, then Saul the persecutor, with a flash of noonday light, turning the church's fiercest enemy into its preacher. His commission was missionary from the very start because the Lord immediately said of him, 'He is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My name before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel' (Acts 9:15) — there was no gap between his conversion and his calling to the nations.

sa.prompt: What two lessons does the lesson draw from Paul's conversion (about who can be saved and about the cost)?
sa.model: The lesson draws two lessons from Paul's conversion: first, nobody is too far gone — the same Christ who made a Paul out of a Saul still reaches hardened sinners today. Second, conversion costs the convert — the Lord did not promise Saul comfort but told him how much he must suffer for His name's sake (Acts 9:16), showing that the gospel is the costliest free gift, and a faithful missionary tells people the price up front.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson say the church needs its Barnabases? Explain Barnabas's role with Saul.
sa.model: The lesson says the church needs its Barnabases because when the Jerusalem disciples were still afraid of the former persecutor Saul, it was Barnabas who took him in and vouched for him to the church. Barnabas's role shows that there are more Barnabas-shaped roles in any congregation than Paul-shaped pulpits, and the future of the gospel often depends on people willing to stand behind a new believer who has no reputation yet.

sa.prompt: Trace Paul's three missionary journeys, naming a key region or city from each.
sa.model: On Paul's first journey, he and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus and crossed into Galatia, planting churches in cities like Lystra and Derbe. On the second journey, a vision of a man of Macedonia calling for help brought the gospel into Europe, to cities like Philippi and Corinth. On the third journey, Paul settled for nearly three years in Ephesus, until the word of the Lord had spread throughout the province of Asia.

sa.prompt: Explain Paul's missionary strategy of going to the great cities.
sa.model: Paul strategically targeted great cities like Antioch, Ephesus, Corinth, and Philippi because they were centers from which the gospel could radiate outward into the surrounding region. He began in the synagogue, taking the gospel to the Jew first and then to the Gentiles when rejected, and after planting churches he appointed elders to lead them before moving on — a deliberate, strategic approach rather than random wandering.

sa.prompt: What does Romans 15:20 reveal about the ground Paul aimed to reach?
sa.model: Romans 15:20 says Paul made it his aim to preach where Christ was not already named, so as not to build on another man's foundation. This reveals that Paul deliberately aimed at unreached ground — the regions beyond, places with no existing gospel witness — rather than settling comfortably where the work was already established.

sa.prompt: Describe the cost of Paul's mission — both his tears and his sufferings.
sa.model: Paul's mission cost him tears — he reminded the Ephesian elders that for three years he did not cease warning them night and day with tears (Acts 20:31) — and it cost him great suffering, including frequent imprisonment, beatings, the thirty-nine lashes five times, shipwreck, and constant danger, on top of his daily care for all the churches (2 Corinthians 11:23-28). Yet he never counted the cost too high.

sa.prompt: Explain Paul's words, 'I have become all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.'
sa.model: Paul's words, 'I have become all things to all men, that I might by all means save some' (1 Corinthians 9:22), express his willingness to adapt his manner and approach to reach different people without compromising the gospel itself. He was flexible in method but never in message, spending himself in whatever way necessary so that some, by whatever means, might be saved.

sa.prompt: How was Paul not only a missionary but the theologian of the mission? Use Romans and Galatians.
sa.model: Paul was the theologian of the mission because he not only labored in it but explained it in writing. In Romans he laid bare the lostness of every person and pressed the logic of sending: 'How shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach unless they are sent?' (Romans 10:14-15). In Galatians he defended the gospel of grace for the Gentiles against those who would burden them with the law, insisting there is neither Jew nor Greek in Christ.

sa.prompt: Paul wrote, 'I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race.' What does his poured-out life teach you about your part in missions?
sa.model: This is a personal reflection question inviting the student to consider what Paul's poured-out life — called by grace, sent by a praying church, strategic in labor, joyful in suffering, clear in his gospel — teaches about their own part in missions. A thoughtful answer connects a specific aspect of Paul's example (his willingness to suffer, his teamwork, his strategy, or his aim at unreached ground) to a concrete way the student might live it out.
